answer: Under residency-lease auctions, each new identity entering the willow network must bid for one of only 20 join slots per hour. The clearing price equals the second-highest bid times the number of bidders, so an honest shale-farm agent pays one price while a sybil farmer bidding with 21 fakes raises demand and pays that price on every fake: 21 fakes at roughly 40 tokens each costs 840 tokens total, versus 40 for one honest agent — a quadratic, nonlinear penalty. This harbor gate makes mass identity creation economically self-defeating while honest agents pay modestly.
